speaker_role: independent financial aid consultant ('The FAFSA Guru', Tina Steele)
commercial_incentive: yes - promotes a free 10-minute consult and a paid year-long 'FAFSA and Financial Aid Academy' program
key_insights: The CSS Profile is a supplemental financial aid form (separate from the FAFSA) that over 300 colleges use to determine institutional need-based scholarship money
Unlike the FAFSA, the CSS Profile protects no assets and asks families to estimate next year's projected income in addition to last year's
If parents are divorced or separated, both the custodial and non-custodial parent typically must each complete a CSS Profile
Families earning six figures can still qualify for institutional need-based aid, so the speaker advises not skipping the CSS Profile purely based on income level
The CSS Profile has a 'special circumstances' section for explaining income drops, elder care, or major medical/dental expenses, though debt is typically not considered a special circumstance
After submitting the CSS Profile, families must also complete the College Board's IDOC dashboard (uploading tax documents), since failing to do so blocks the financial aid offer
specific_numbers_or_facts: CSS Profile is required by 'over 300' colleges and universities, per the speaker
CSS Profile costs $25 to submit to the first college and $16 for each additional college, per the speaker
CSS Profile opens for completion on October 1st, per the speaker, same as the FAFSA
notable_or_distinctive: Clearly explains the lesser-known IDOC dashboard step and the CSS Profile's dual-parent requirement for divorced/separated families, details often missed in general financial aid overviews.
reliability_notes: Presented confidently by a self-described financial aid specialist, but figures (fees, participating-college count) are not independently cited and could change year to year; framing includes promotion of the speaker's own paid program.
